pr_title: [GUI] Kill skin timers thread, move to ProcessSlow
pr_body:
## Description
This fixes the race condition/use-after-free introduced with the skin timers addition by killing the separate thread while moving the processing logic to CApp ProcessSlow (same time interval as the original thread).
Completely untested, I have no way of checking this for the following days, just checking if it builds and maybe get a testbuild.

## Motivation and context
Fix https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/21791

## How has this been tested?
Runtime tested on macOS

## What is the effect on users?
Fix use after free
pr_comments:
Runtime tested on osx with the jenkins testbuild. All good.
Detected an unrelated issue with the debug overlay (it's duplicated if the player is running), will check if after https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/21795 the issue persists.
@enen92  can you please squash down to a single commit? Only if you like, ofc.
I think it's fine as is, second commit has no relation with what's being done on the first one.

> moving the processing logic to CApp ProcessSlow (same time interval as the original thread).

Time interval was 500 ms before but now is ~16 ms because has NOT moved to `ProcessSlow` but `CApplication::Process()` 

I mean that skin timers are evaluated every 16 ms and not seems necessary 🤔

Anyway tested on Windows and Shield and is working fine.

> NOT moved to ProcessSlow but CApplication::Process()

 Yikes. Good catch. Overlooked that in my review, sorry.
Agrf, thanks @thexai will try to push it in a while.

issue_context.title: Race condition in CGUIInfoManager causing an user-after-free
issue_context.body:
<!--- Please fill out this template to the best of your ability. You can always edit this issue once you have created it. -->
<!--- Read the following link before you create a new problem report: https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Submit_a_bug_report  -->
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
The problem is that `CGUIInfoManager::m_multiInfo` is modified from multiple threads causing a reallocation of the `std::vector`s internal buffer while a different thread has a reference to an object inside that buffer.

Here are the logs and Address Sanitizer output of two occasions:

#### Crash on startup

Debug log: https://gist.github.com/neo1973/1e72f91a0f5bd4d495e9088981cf0700
ASAN output: https://gist.github.com/neo1973/e2c546d82f0e87e870228c614491bf76

#### Crash while navigating through GUI:

Debug log: https://gist.github.com/neo1973/fd16b4f454fb3ac5a49c1408b7d80ae8
ASAN output: https://gist.github.com/neo1973/0960636f540c6c6f6860b3ee8fe40380

The issue is best reproduced when I launch Kodi with these ASAN options: `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_stack_use_after_return=1:fast_unwind_on_malloc=0 ./kodi-wayland`
This makes the timings just right (on my machine) to trigger the bug within a couple of seconds, most of the time even before the GUI is up.

## Expected Behavior
No undefined behaviour that can cause crashes.

## Actual Behavior
Undefined behaviour and possible crashes.

## Possible Fix
Difficult. Simply protecting `CGUIInfoManager::m_multiInfo` with a `CCriticalSection` causes deadlocks. It doesn't matter if the `m_critInfo` one is reused or a separate `CCriticalSection` is added.

### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
<!--- Provide a link to a live example, or an unambiguous set of steps to -->
<!--- reproduce this bug. Include code to reproduce, if relevant -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
Happens immediately on startup or shortly after while browsing through the GUI. I don't think any particular steps are required to hit the problem.

### Debuglog

<!--- A debuglog is always mandatory when creating an issue. Provide one! -->
The debuglog can be found here: See above

comments:
@enen92  `CSkinTimerManager`'s worker thread calls into not threadsafe `CGUIInfoManager`! GUIInfoManager must not be called from other threads than the main thread.

EDIT: Well, `CGUIInfoManager` has a member `m_critSecition`, however, implementation seems not to use this to protect access to `m_multiInfo` - by design? Or is this a bug? ... Can of worms, I'd say.

I was not a big fan of having the skin timer evaluation in its own thread to be honest, it kinda foresee this would eventually happen. Screen timers just registers a few more info conditions into the infomanager, maybe we can simply register callbacks for them.
Will take a look but unfortunately I won't be near a computer until next week.
My preferred solution would be to get rid of the thread in `CSkinTimerManager` and to call the functionality currently located in `CSkinTimerManager::Process` from `CApplication::ProcessSlow()`.

review_comments: Not sure we still need `m_timerCriticalSection` as we are not calling `CSkinTimerManager`from other threads than the main thread anymore.
shouldn't be needed anymore, it's all called from the main thread now. Added a note to doxy docs warning about this.
